Synopsis:
    Fed Chair Kevin Warsh signaled at the Jackson Hole conference that a rate hike is likely needed to bring inflation back to the 2% target, catching markets off guard with his hawkishness. The Fed meets September 15-16, with markets pricing roughly 2:1 odds of a 25bps hike. Warsh now faces a credibility test: follow through with a hike or risk being seen as inconsistent. Political pressure from Trump (who wants lower rates) and pre-midterm election sensitivity add complexity. Key August jobs and CPI data will be pivotal inputs before the decision. Rates have been held at 3.50%-3.75% since December, with 3 of 12 voting members already dissenting in favor of a hike at the July meeting.
